title: Extend the egress guard to non-provider egress (webhook delivery)
background: Model providers are not the only path content leaves the box. An audit of every outbound Req call in lib/ found: anthropic.ex:139 and embedding_client.ex:109,133 are gated by Admission; workers/content_ingestion_worker.ex:634 (Req.get of an arbitrary ingestion URL) bypasses it and is guarded instead by UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 + redirect: false (:620-632); verification/github_actions.ex:17, secrets/fly_adapter.ex:60,112, cli/client.ex:93 (a Req.request to a CONFIGURABLE loopctl server, carrying JSON bodies - omitted from the round-1 inventory) and webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43 all bypass Admission entirely. Of these, webhook delivery is the one that can carry TENANT CONTENT to a TENANT-SUPPLIED URL. The 2026-07-15 draft missed this: a local_only guarantee that covers embeddings and extraction but not webhooks is not a guarantee. CORRECTION to that inventory: webhook delivery bypasses ADMISSION but is NOT otherwise unguarded - req_delivery.ex:20 calls UrlGuard.pin/1 and :31 uses pinned_request_opts with redirect: false, and UrlGuard blocks loopback, private, CGNAT, link-local and Fly 6PN targets to close GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg. So today a loopback webhook destination returns {:error, "blocked_url: :blocked_ip"}, and a local_only tenant - who by definition needs a private-range or tenant-declared destination - is blocked by the SSRF guard rather than by the locality guard. This story therefore does not add a URL policy; it routes webhook delivery through the SINGLE policy module from US-41.4 AC-41.4.9, which composes the SSRF denylist with the allowlist/tenant-declaration carve-outs.

story.as_a: a tenant who marked a scope local_only
story.i_want_to: have that marking cover EVERY path content can leave the instance, including webhook delivery
story.so_that: the guarantee I was given is the guarantee I actually have - not one that holds for two subsystems and silently fails for a third

rationale: A privacy guarantee is only as strong as its weakest egress path. Shipping US-41.4 alone would let loopctl truthfully report 'all providers local' while a webhook subscription ships article bodies to an arbitrary internet host. This story closes the gap and, just as importantly, makes the posture report honest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Webhook delivery consults the SAME single egress policy module as US-41.4 (AC-41.4.9) - the one that composes UrlGuard's SSRF denylist with the deployment allowlist and the tenant's declared trusted endpoints. For a local_only scope, a delivery whose destination is not classified local (network-local or tenant-declared) is refused before the request, with the same fail-closed semantics (unclassifiable means refuse). Conversely a destination that IS allowlisted or tenant-declared must become deliverable, which it is not today: req_delivery.ex:20's unconditional UrlGuard.pin/1 currently rejects every loopback/private destination, so this story replaces that call with the policy module rather than adding a second policy beside it. Scope precedence follows US-41.4 AC-41.4.2 (most-restrictive-wins; a subscription with no project follows the tenant marking). Tenant declarations are PURPOSE-SCOPED per AC-41.4.5 constraint 2: only a declaration carrying the 'webhook' purpose makes a destination deliverable here - a host declared for an Ollama inference box does NOT authorize POSTing tenant content to it. And per AC-41.4.9 a tenant declaration carves NOTHING out of the SSRF denylist; only the operator-controlled deployment allowlist can make a private-range destination reachable.

A blocked delivery is NOT a silent drop and NOT an infinite retry: the event is recorded as blocked with an agent-readable reason, surfaced through the existing webhook delivery/failure surfaces, so the tenant can see that a subscription is incompatible with their local_only marking.

Creating or updating a webhook subscription with a non-local destination on an already-local_only scope is rejected AT CONFIG TIME with a legible remediation, rather than accepted and silently blocked at delivery time.

Marking a scope local_only when incompatible webhook subscriptions already exist does not silently break them: the operation either refuses with a list of the offending subscriptions or completes and reports them explicitly. Which one is chosen is documented; a silent state change is not acceptable.

egress_posture (US-41.4 AC-41.4.8) is extended to report webhook destinations and their local classification (network-local vs tenant-declared vs non-local), so the posture report covers every content-carrying egress path. Until this story lands, the posture report must state that its scope is provider calls only.

The remaining outbound paths are explicitly triaged in the docs with a rationale for each, and the triage list must MATCH the AC-41.4.4 static check's findings exactly - any call site the check reports that has no triage entry is a review failure: ingestion URL fetch (workers/content_ingestion_worker.ex:634 - inbound content, sends no tenant data, already URL-guarded), GitHub verification (verification/github_actions.ex:17 - commit metadata only), Fly secrets (secrets/fly_adapter.ex:60,112 - operator-plane, no tenant content), and cli/client.ex:93 (the loopctl CLI's own client: it targets the CONFIGURED loopctl server, is not a tenant-content egress path to a third party, and runs outside the request path - it is exempted by an explicit entry in the wrapper allowlist rather than being silently unmatched by the static check). Any that DO carry tenant content are brought under the guard rather than documented away. All of them - including the ingestion fetch - consult the single policy module, so no path keeps a private copy of the URL rules.

Any new table or column introduced by this story (blocked-delivery records, per-subscription locality classification) carries tenant_id, uses the enable_rls/1 macro (ENABLE, not FORCE, per CLAUDE.md's Multi-Tenant Rules), and has a tenant-isolation test asserting tenant A cannot read tenant B's blocked-delivery records.

test_cases.name: local_only blocks a public webhook destination
preconditions: subscription pointing at a public, undeclared URL
expected_results: delivery recorded as blocked with a legible reason

test_cases.name: allowlisted / tenant-declared destination still delivers
preconditions: subscription pointing at a destination present in the deployment allowlist (or declared as a tenant trusted endpoint) - NOT a bare loopback URL, which UrlGuard blocks by default
expected_results: and a control case: the same private-range host WITHOUT an allowlist/declaration entry is still refused by the SSRF policy - GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg stays closed

test_cases.name: incompatible subscription rejected at creation
steps: create a subscription with a public destination
expected_results: rejected with remediation naming the conflict

test_cases.name: pre-existing subscriptions surfaced when enabling local_only
preconditions: scope with a public webhook subscription
expected_results: the offending subscriptions are reported explicitly per the documented behavior - never silently disabled

test_cases.name: blocked deliveries do not retry forever
expected_results: no unbounded retry backlog - blocked is terminal for that delivery

test_cases.name: blocked-delivery records are tenant-isolated
preconditions: two tenants, one with blocked deliveries
steps: read blocked-delivery records as the other tenant

technical_notes: webhooks/req_delivery.ex:20 (UrlGuard.pin/1) and :31 (pinned_request_opts, redirect: false) are the existing guard; :43 issues the request. The change is to replace the direct UrlGuard call with the US-41.4 policy module at the point the destination is resolved, mirroring the provider-call placement. Do NOT weaken the default denylist - the carve-out is allowlist/declaration-driven only.
Webhook signing secrets are already Cloak-encrypted (webhooks/webhook.ex:61); the destination URL is not a secret and must be readable by egress_posture.

Do not conflate 'blocked' with 'failed' in the delivery record - a blocked delivery is a configuration conflict, and an operator or agent reading failures needs to tell them apart. Note there are now TWO block reasons to distinguish: SSRF-denied (policy) and locality-denied (local_only).

AC-41.5.6 is a real audit, not a paragraph: re-run the outbound Req call inventory at implementation time, since new call sites may have landed. The US-41.4 AC-41.4.4 static check makes that inventory mechanical.
